tool.title: Does a path or bean exist on main or any open PR
tool.description: Answer whether a path, a path prefix or a bean id appears on a repository's default branch or on the head of any of its open pull requests, and where: the PR number, head branch, first commit author and creation time. A path or prefix matches files at the default branch and files each open PR changes; a bean id matches PR titles, bodies and head branch names. Repositories or PRs that could not be read are listed, so an empty answer is never mistaken for absence.

inputs.name: prefix
inputs.description: A directory or file-name prefix; every path under or starting with it matches.

inputs.name: bean
inputs.description: A bean id, full or short.

inputs.name: repo
inputs.description: Repositories to search. Repeat. Defaults to the current checkout's origin.

outputs.name: lookup
outputs.description: One line per hit: repository, default branch or PR number, head, author, when, and what matched. Then what could not be read. Exactly one of path, prefix or bean must be given. With --json, `definitions.lookup` of schemas/skills/bean-drain/output.schema.json.

outputs.name: result
outputs.description: With --json, the hits as one `OpenWorkLookup` record, with what could not be read. Programs read this; people read `lookup`.

selection.when: Before starting work that a sibling may already have in flight, and before publishing that a path or a piece of work does not exist.
selection.limits: Open PRs only, not unpushed local branches or closed PRs. It uses the GitHub REST API, not GraphQL, because cloud sessions are refused GraphQL. A PR's changed-file list is capped by the API at 3000 files; a bigger PR is listed under unread rather than guessed. For the current checkout alone, `git show origin/main:<path>` in its own command is enough.
selection.cost: One paged REST listing of open PRs per repository, plus one files listing per open PR for a path or prefix query.

remedies.none: No declared Tool lists open PRs another way. A session with the GitHub MCP server can list them with `list_pull_requests` and read each one's files.

$comment.comment:
The Tool node for "does this exist anywhere reachable", bean `pomp`.

pomp's three cases: a branch older than the claim (ask the remote), a fetch
in the same command as the read (separate them), and the file existing only
on an open PR's head, which no skill line can cover because it needs the PR
list. The owner said "wait" on 2026-10-22 until a second session hit case 3.
f1e1 on 2026-10-24 was that session, and the owner reopened pomp (choice B).

The bean-id query is what `bean-claim-check` calls. The path and prefix
queries are what an agent calls before it publishes that something does
not exist (`issue-working`), or before it builds a module a sibling may
already have in flight.

@module tools/open-work-lookup
